content: These references include studies, reviews, and analyses related to pharmaceutical policies, pricing, cost containment, and the impact of generic drug use across various countries and healthcare systems. 1. A study conducted in Belgium examined the impact of generic competition on the sales of cholesterol-lowering medications, antidepressants, and acid-blocking agents. The findings were published in Acta Clin Belg in 2012. 2. Fraeyman et al. (2013) analyzed the evolution of co-payment systems and the market share of generic medications within the Belgian reference pricing system. Their research was published in Applied Health Economics and Health Policy. 3. Fu, Li, and Yip (2018) investigated both the intended and unintended consequences of price changes for drugs and medical services in China. Their findings were published in Social Science & Medicine. 4. Gaebel, Toeg, and Levine (2008) explored the clinical and economic effects of a therapeutic substitution policy for proton pump inhibitors among Aboriginal patients in Canada’s Northwest Territories. This study was published in Disease Management and Health Outcomes. 5. Galizzi, Ghislandi, and Miraldo (2011) reviewed the effects of reference pricing in pharmaceutical markets, with their findings published in PharmacoEconomics. 6. Garuoliene et al. (2011) presented a case study of Lithuania, demonstrating how small European countries can achieve low drug prices. Their research was published in Expert Review of Pharmacoeconomics & Outcomes Research. 7. Ghislandi, Armeni, and Jommi (2013) evaluated the impact of generic reference pricing in Italy over a decade. Their findings were published in the European Journal of Health Economics. 8. Ghislandi, Krulichova, and Garattini (2005) discussed structural changes in Italy’s pharmaceutical policy, with their analysis published in Health Policy. 9. Gilman and Kautter (2007) examined consumer responses to dual incentives under multi-tiered prescription drug formularies, with their findings published in the American Journal of Managed Care. 10. Gilman and Kautter (2008) also studied the impact of multi-tiered co-payments on prescription drug use and costs among Medicare beneficiaries, publishing their results in Health Services Research. 11. Godman et al. (2013) reviewed reforms and initiatives in Scotland aimed at encouraging generic drug prescribing, discussing their influence and implications for other countries. This study was published in Expert Review of Pharmacoeconomics & Outcomes Research. 12. Godman et al. (2009) analyzed the impact of recent reforms in Austria on the utilization and expenditure of proton pump inhibitors and lipid-lowering drugs, with implications for future policies. Their findings were published in Expert Review of Pharmacoeconomics & Outcomes Research. 13. Godman et al. (2010) compared policies across Europe designed to enhance prescribing efficiency by increasing generic drug utilization. Their findings were published in Frontiers in Pharmacology and Expert Review of Pharmacoeconomics & Outcomes Research. 14. Godman et al. (2013) evaluated the influence of multiple initiatives in Sweden to improve prescribing efficiency for angiotensin receptor blockers following the introduction of generic losartan. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Clinical Practice. 15. Godman et al. (2009) assessed the impact of reforms across 20 European countries aimed at improving the quality and efficiency of statin prescribing. Their findings were published in Basic & Clinical Pharmacology & Toxicology. 16. Goldberg et al. (2012) conducted a retrospective analysis of generic dispensing rates, gross costs, and drug therapy continuation rates following the implementation of a value formulary. Their findings were published in the Journal of Managed Care Pharmacy. 17. Gomez-Dantes et al. (2012) described the establishment of a new entity in Mexico for negotiating public procurement prices for patented medicines. Their findings were published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization. 18. Gorsh et al. (2011) evaluated the economic impact of co-payment waivers on a generic-to-generic conversion program, with their findings published in the Journal of Managed Care Pharmacy. 19. Grootendorst and Stewart (2006) re-examined the impact of reference pricing on antihypertensive drug expenditures in British Columbia, publishing their findings in Health Economics. 20. Grootendorst et al. (2004) analyzed the effects of differential cost-sharing for non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs on the use and costs of analgesic medications. Their findings were published in a research paper on the social and economic dimensions of an aging population. 21. Guan et al. (2018) conducted an interrupted time-series analysis to evaluate the impact of generic market entry for antineoplastic products in China. Their findings were published in BMJ Open. 22. Guan et al. (2018) also studied the effects of implementing a low-price medicine policy on drug prices in China, publishing their findings in the International Journal of Health Planning and Management. 23. Hakonsen et al. (2009) reviewed the achievements of price control strategies for pharmaceutical cost containment in Norway between 1994 and 2004. Their findings were published in Health Policy. 24. Han et al. (2015) examined the effects of pharmaceutical cost containment policies on doctors’ prescribing behavior, focusing on antibiotics. Their findings were published in Health Policy. 25. Han et al. (2013) conducted a case study on the impact of price controls on antibacterial expenditures in 12 Chinese hospitals from 1996 to 2005. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Health Services. 26. Hay (2013) discussed the competitive tendering process for purchasing factor concentrates in the 21st century, with findings published in Haemophilia. 27. Hinrichs et al. (2014) provided insights for the NHS on procurement and supply chain management through a rapid evidence assessment. 28. Hoffmann et al. (2009) evaluated the impact of rebate contracts promoting generic drug substitution on doctors’ prescribing practices, with findings published in Deutsches Ärzteblatt International. 29. Holmes et al. (2010) analyzed the use of generic antiretroviral agents and associated cost savings in PEPFAR treatment programs, publishing their findings in JAMA. 30. Hornyak et al. (2019) studied price competition and reimbursement of biosimilar granulocyte-colony stimulating factors in Hungary, with findings published in Expert Review of Pharmacoeconomics & Outcomes Research. 31. Hornyák et al. (2017) shared experiences with price competition for biosimilar drugs in Hungary, publishing their findings in Value in Health. 32. Hsiao et al. (2010) examined the effects of price regulation, new market entry, and information shocks on Taiwan’s pharmaceutical market from 2001 to 2004. Their findings were published in BMC Health Services Research. 33. Johnson et al. (2011) conducted a five-year analysis of utilization and drug cost outcomes associated with benefit design changes, including reference pricing for proton pump inhibitors, in a state employee health plan. Their findings were published in the Journal of Managed Care Pharmacy. 34. Kaiser et al. (2010) reviewed the regulation of pharmaceutical prices in Denmark, focusing on evidence from a reference price reform. Their findings were published in a discussion paper from the University of Copenhagen. 35. Kalo et al. (2007) evaluated the cost-containment effects of therapeutic reference pricing in Hungary, publishing their findings in Health Policy. 36. Kaplan et al. (2012) reviewed policies promoting generic medicine use in lowand middle-income countries, with findings published in Health Policy. 37. Kenneally and Walshe (2012) discussed Ireland’s recent experience with pharmaceutical cost-containment policies and their sustainability, publishing their findings in Value in Health. 38. Kim and Skordis-Worrall (2017) analyzed whether voluntary pooled procurement could reduce the price of antiretroviral drugs, using efavirenz as a case study. Their findings were published in Health Policy and Planning. 39. Kohler et al. (2015) examined the impact of pharmaceutical pricing transparency in Brazil’s public procurement system, publishing their findings in Global Health. 40. Koskinen et al. (2014) studied the impact of reference pricing and generic substitution on the daily cost of antipsychotic medications in Finland, with findings published in Health Economics Review. 41. Koskinen et al. (2015) conducted a time-series analysis on the effects of generic substitution and reference pricing on antipsychotic costs in Finland, publishing their findings in Value in Health. 42. Kwon et al. (2019) analyzed the effects of massive price cuts on drug expenditures in Korea, publishing their findings in Health Policy. 43. Kwon et al. (2013) studied the impact of price cuts on drug spending in South Korea, focusing on antihyperlipidemic agents. Their findings were published in Health Policy. 44. Langley et al. (2018) evaluated a price transparency intervention for two commonly prescribed medications and its impact on institutional expenditure. Their findings were published in the Future Healthcare Journal. 45. Law et al. (2011) assessed the short-term impact of Ontario’s generic pricing reforms, publishing their findings in PLoS ONE. 46. Lee et al. (2013) evaluated the success of Argentina’s generic drug law, publishing their findings in Value in Health. 47. Lee et al. (2012) examined the effects of new pricing and co-payment schemes for pharmaceuticals in South Korea, publishing their findings in Health Policy. 48. Lee et al. (2015) conducted a systematic review of international experiences in controlling pharmaceutical expenditures, publishing their findings in the Journal of Health Services Research & Policy. 49. Lee et al. (2012) reviewed the implications of reference pricing for U.S. prescription drug spending, publishing their findings in the American Journal of Managed Care. 50. Lee et al. (2006) analyzed the impact of cost-containment strategies on pharmaceutical expenditures under Taiwan’s national health insurance system from 1996 to 2003, publishing their findings in PharmacoEconomics. 51. Leopold et al. (2012) compared the impact of external price referencing on medicine prices across 14 European countries, publishing their findings in the Southern Medical Review. 52. Lessing et al. (2015) conducted a natural experiment in New Zealand to evaluate the outcomes of patients switching brands due to generic reference pricing, publishing their findings in Administration and Policy in Mental Health. 53. Li et al. (2013) evaluated the introduction and impact of China’s national essential medicines scheme in three provinces, publishing their findings in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization. 54. Lin (2011) assessed the impact of a reference-based pricing program for select drug classes, publishing findings in the Journal of Managed Care Pharmacy. 55. Lu et al. (2013) analyzed changes in the use of antidiabetic medications following price regulations in China from 1999 to 2009, publishing their findings in the Journal of Pharmaceutical Health Services Research. 56. Lunte et al. (2015) discussed efforts to reduce the price of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis treatment through the Global Drug Facility, publishing their findings in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization. 57. Maiga and Williams-Jones (2010) assessed the impact of market regulation on the price of essential medicines in Mali’s private sector, publishing their findings in Health Policy. 58. Mardetko et al. (2017) evaluated the cost-saving potential of therapeutic reference pricing for proton pump inhibitors in Slovenia, publishing their findings in the International Journal of Clinical Pharmacy. 59. Mardetko and Kos (2017) analyzed the economic consequences of introducing therapeutic reference pricing in Slovenia, publishing their findings in the European Journal of Health Economics. 60. Mardetko et al. (2017) reviewed the development and performance of Slovenia’s external reference pricing system from 2007 to 2012, publishing their findings in Health Policy and Technology. 61. McCabe et al. (2010) argued against continuing the multiple sclerosis risk-sharing scheme, publishing their findings in BMJ. 62. Milovanovic et al. (2004) shared lessons from a drug tender in a teaching hospital in a transition country, publishing their findings in the European Journal of Clinical Pharmacology. 63. Mishuk et al. (2019) conducted a systematic review of federal and state generic drug policies and their impact on drug use, spending, and patient outcomes, publishing their findings in Research in Social and Administrative Pharmacy. 64. Mohamed and Kreling (2016) analyzed the impact of a pricing policy change on retail medicine prices in Egypt, publishing their findings in Value in Health Regional Issues. 65. Moorkens et al. (2019) examined the influence of policy measures on market dynamics for biosimilar and originator infliximab in Swedish hospitals, publishing their findings in BioDrugs. 66. Moorkens et al. (2019) also studied the market dynamics for biosimilar and originator etanercept in outpatient settings in Sweden, publishing their findings in BioDrugs. 67. Moreno-Torres et al. (2011) evaluated the impact of repeated cost-containment policies on pharmaceutical expenditures in Spain, publishing their findings in the European Journal of Health Economics. 68. Morgan et al. (2009) compared tiered formularies and reference pricing policies, publishing their findings in Open Medicine. 69. Moye-Holz et al. (2017) discussed policy approaches to improve the availability and affordability of medicines in Mexico, publishing their findings in Global Health.
